segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending weekly number 36. 35 trending open source projects on GitHub right now. Let's go.
Wrangling complex clawed code sessions usually means constantly checking text percentages to see when your context
window is about to overflow. Ghosty black hole turns your context limits into a literal rayraced black hole
inside your terminal. It uses a custom ghosty shader to gravitationally lens and distort your terminal text live as
your token count fills up. Running compact shrinks the hole back to a tiny seed in the corner.
You don't need a heavy Python environment or a Docker container just to extract clean markdown from a PDF.
Light do runs as a zero setup clientside web utility. It handles multicolumn layouts and latex math equations
natively in your browser. A custom layout engine groups text mathematically so your multicolumn PDFs don't scramble when you copy paste them into claude.
Prompt engineering was about getting one good answer. Loop engineering is the next layer. Designing the whole system that prompts and orchestrates an AI
coding agent through many cycles of plan, act, check, and correct. This repo is a practical reference for exactly
that. The patterns for building durable agent loops. Drawing on work from Adi Osmani and Anthropics Boris Churnney.
AI agents default to generating code.
Ponytail makes your agent ask whether it should before writing anything. The skill forces it to reason like the laziest senior developer in the room.
The one who knows the best code is the code you never wrote. Can this be done by deleting something? Reusing what
exists, not building it at all? Less code? Less surface area? Fewer bugs. The senior engineer instinct bottled into a skill.
Watching your AI coding agent lose its mind the second a session goes past 50 steps is the worst part of vibe coding.
MIMO code fixes this agent amnesia on long horizon programming tasks. Built as a fork of open code, this terminal
native assistant uses SQLite powered cross- session memory to store project state across dozens of turns. It even
compiles natural language skill files into deterministic JavaScript so your task execution never gets flaky.
Using your most capable model for every task, burns budget on work that doesn't need it. Improve from Shad CN splits the
job intelligently. The expensive Frontier model audits your code base and writes detailed execution plans. The cheaper, faster models carry those plans
out. Frontier quality direction at a fraction of the token cost. The senior architect thinks the junior developers type.
You want a slick animated background for a video, a site header, or an album cover. And your options are paying for stock loops or fighting a 3D app for an
hour. Lumen just makes it. It's a generative shader studio that runs in your browser with nine WebGL 2 art modes, liquid chrome, silk, halftone,
dataglyphs, and more. Every animation is a perfect seamless loop and you export straight to PNG, webm or GIF. No watermark, no account.
Runway and Pika do gorgeous AI video editing, but they're closed and they charge per generation. Bite Dance just open sourced a serious alternative.
Bernini is a unified video generation and editing framework that splits the job in two. An MLMbased planner built on
Quen 2.5VL reasons over your text, images, and source video and decides what should change. Then a DIT renderer
built on one 2.2 paints the actual frames.
Setting up a fresh Windows machine for development is a half day of pain.
Install git, the right runtimes, your editors, your CLIs, tweak a dozen settings, and inevitably forget
something. Windows Developer Config automates the whole thing. It's an official tool that scripts the setup and
configuration of your Windows dev environment. So, a new box goes from blank to ready with one repeatable run instead of an afternoon of clicking through installers.
Building a slide deck in PowerPoint is a great way to lose a whole day to manual formatting and pixel pushing. PPT Master
is a clawed skill that builds full presentations from a single prompt. It reads your raw spec file to structure the slides, then writes Python code to
generate the actual deck. Because it uses the Python PPTX library, every single element in the final output is fully editable.
Building separate reinforcement learning pipelines every time you need to post-train different model architectures is a massive waste of engineering
cycles. UNIRL solves this by providing a unified reinforcement learning infrastructure across completely
different model families. It lets you apply a single postraining loop to everything from standard text LLMs to diffusion image generators.
That slot machine text where numbers and letters roll and tumble into place looks fantastic on counters, scoreboards, and
price tickers. And people usually reach for a heavy animation library to get it.
Slot text needs none. It's a dependencyfree text roll animation that works in vanilla JavaScript, React, and
Vue. All three. Drop it in, point it at some text, and your numbers spin into place with that satisfying mechanical
roll. Running million token context windows on standard attention kernels is a fast way to watch your GPU memory
explode and your prefill crawl to a halt.
MSA fixes this by bringing a blockwise sparse attention kernel specifically co-designed for ultraong context. Built
upon grouped query attention, it scores key value blocks using a lightweight index branch.
Wrangling massive stacks of qualitative research transcripts or user feedback usually means endless hours of manual coding or settling for sketchy uncalibrated AI summaries.
Concord acts as an open-source research tool designed for instrument grade text analysis. It packages gold standard calibration and statistical correction models into a local workflow.
Building an AI app today means duct taping three databases together.
Postgress for your data, pine cone for vectors, and a graph DB for relationships. Then babysitting all three. Helix DB collapses that into one.
It's an open-source OOLTP graph vector database built from scratch in Rust with graph traversal, vector search, and its
own strongly typed query language, Helix QL, in a single engine.
Submitting a research paper only to have a peer reviewer instantly destroy it over obvious gaps is a miserable waste
of your time. Paper Jury lets you run a brutal presubmission stress test right in your terminal. It is a local clawed code skill that turns feedback into a
closed loop. It triages critiques as either autofixable text edits or major research decisions, keeping the final
judgment calls strictly with you. When you ask a coding agent to plan a feature or diagram an architecture, you usually
get a wall of markdown or a tangled mess of boxes. Effective HTML does it cleanly. It's an agent skill that makes
clawed code or codecs produce elegant, simple HTML plans and architecture diagrams. Readable layouts you can
actually share with your team instead of squinting at ASKI art.
Commercial Smartome sensors are sleek, soulless, and locked to an app. Velt model 01 goes the other way. It's an
ESP32 powered environmental monitor with a retro inpired design and a crisp e- in display reading temperature, humidity,
and air pressure off your room and showing them on a screen that sips power and never glares. Connect it to Wi-Fi and it pulls the current time, too.
Reviewing a massive multifile code change generated by an AI agent inside a raw terminal diff is a painful exercise.
Builder.io/skills fixes this by giving your agents the ability to generate human optimized visual recaps. It adds
custom commands like visual recap directly to clawed code or cursor. Your agents can output rich NDX diagrams and
clear status signals so you actually understand their architecture changes before hitting approve.
Every blog post needs a header image and you're stuck choosing between cheesy stock photos or generic AI art that
looks like everyone else's. ELO gives you a house style instead. It's an AI agent skill that turns an idea or a
whole article into an original print style editorial illustration, the kind you'd see in a magazine starring a recurring mascot, so your images feel like a consistent brand.
Vervoice is an LLM based texttospech engine, and this is its narration focused build. Instead of the choppy
delivery most open TTS gives you, it's tuned for long form reading, audiobooks, explainers, documentation with stable voice identity across a whole passage.
It does zeroot voice cloning from a prompt clip with a two pass speaker refinement mode that cuts accent leakage when you clone across languages.
Nullframe is a live telemetry dashboard built in the Nothing design language.
That stark monochrome dot matrix aesthetic from the nothing phones. CPU, memory, network, all your live system
stats rendered in clean black and white with that distinctive glyph styling. So your monitoring screen actually looks like a designed object instead of task manager.
Watching your autonomous agent drift into an infinite 500step spiral while burning your API credits is the most stressful part of building with LLMs.
Agent Harness fixes this by acting as an open-source evaluation framework for long horizon agent loops. It tracks
every step, letting you run small local models as verifiers to validate structured tool calls before hitting expensive APIs.
T-Mreen are everywhere, but they predate modern terminals, and it shows clunky rendering, no graphics, decades old
internals. Buu is a screen style terminal multipplexer built on lib ghost t, the engine behind Mitchell Hashimoto's ghosty terminal, so you get
persistent sessions and split panes backed by a fast modern rendering core instead of a 1990s codebase.
Running your agent loops on third party cloud platforms usually means sending all your proprietary files and API keys
to someone else's servers. Onfable runs terminal commands and edits code files, but everything stays inside your local directory. Since it's fully model
neutral, you can plug in claude or your own self-hosted endpoint with one command.
Zod is the validation library half the TypeScript world runs on, but it has a cost. Every validation builds and walks
the schema at runtime on every single request. Zod compiler moves that work to build time. It compiles your ZOD schemas
into plain zero overhead validation functions ahead of time. So at runtime there's no schema interpretation left, just a tight function doing the checks.
Someone vibe coded an entire World of Warcraft style MMO RPG with Claude Fable 5 and it actually works online with
friends. World of Clawed Craft is fully open source and the procedural generation is the wild part.
timberframed houses, animated lakes, drifting clouds, real-time shadows, and 12 rigged creature families with walk, attack, and death animations.
Power level 10K spoiled everyone with that gorgeous information dense shell prompt. Coralane brings the same energy
to Claude Code status line. It's a richly styled status bar for your Claude Code sessions, and the install is the clever part. You paste one prompt. The
AI interviews you about what you want shown and how it should look, then configures and installs it for you.
If you've tried running clawed code with anything other than Anthropic's flagship models, you already know how quickly those agentic loops fall apart.
Open code harness gives you a clean room model agnostic harness built from scratch. It lets you swap out expensive
API endpoints for openw weight local models like Gemma or Quen without breaking your tool calling logic.
Instead of trusting a single polished response that hides all the model uncertainty, you can pit your LLMs against each other. Council is an
open-source native Mac OS app that lets you run parallel debates. You ask one question and up to nine models answer in
parallel. They critique each other blind, giving you custom personas like a devil's advocate to stress test their logic.
Apple shipped the foundation models framework so you can build with their ondevice LLM, but the real world patterns for using it well are still
being figured out. Apple just published their own. Foundation models utilities is an official collection of emerging
and experimental patterns for building on the foundation models framework. the techniques Apple's own engineers are using that haven't made it into the
formal docs yet. We all know Claude Fable is a beast at high level planning, but burning those premium tokens on
actual code construction is a massive waste. Architect Loop fixes this by splitting the workload. It uses Fable as
a master architect to spec tasks and freeze readonly acceptance gates. Then it dispatches GPT 5.5 codecs as a cheap
parallel builder to write the code, saving you 80% on tokens.
Instead of gluing together five separate tools to distill and serve your own custom LLMs, you can manage the entire
pipeline inside Tessera. This from scratch engine handles FSDP distillation from a large teacher model, then
compiles custom Triton kernels for serving. Speculative decoding and paged KV batching run right out of the box with a Rust gateway managing production
traffic and Jax tools for model interpretability.
Every time your coding agent sends a request, it ships a huge wall of code context and you pay for every token of
it, even the parts the model didn't need. Token Tamer trims that on the way out. It's a drop-in proxy that
compresses bloated code context in real time. The claim is 50 to 80% fewer tokens without dropping what the model
actually needs to answer. In a real compose app, your navigation logic is scattered across a dozen files and nobody can see the whole flow at once.
Compose nav graph is an Android Studio plugin that visualizes your entire app as an interactive map. Every screen
rendered as a live preview, the typed arguments each one takes, and the transitions between them, all laid out as a graph you can actually navigate.
